newsitem.title: UK: BA says services returning to normal.
newsitem.headline: BA says services returning to normal.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday its longhaul operations were running a 100 percent service as the number of cabin crew on sick leave during the recent industrial dispute continued to fall sharply.
European flights from Heathrow are running at 98 percent and should be back to 100 percent within 10 days, the airline said in a statement.
Services from Gatwick, international flights from UK regional airports and all UK domestic routes are running a full 100 percent schedule.
BA said in view of the recent exceptional levels of sick leave, it intended to "review its sickness policies and procedures in cabin crew" and would seek the views and advice from employees.

To speed the return to full services, BA has introduced a fast-track training programme for cabin crew recruits. This will enable flying duties to start after an initial 22 days' training instead of 35 days previously.
On Monday, BA said last month's cabin crew strike would cost the company 125 million stg.
